dedupe_keys.name: cinch1 covid 19 infection control in hospitals a staff physical distancing model

description: CINCH1 is a prototype model of physical distancing among staff at University College London Hospital during the Covid-19 pandemic, developed at the School of Geography of the University of Leeds. Groups of agents move through simple spaces under conflicting motives: reaching their destination, keeping physical distance from each other and walking together with a companion. It draws on the Capability, Opportunity and Motivation of Behaviour (COM-B) framework of the UCL Centre for Behaviour Change and is meant to inform behavioural interventions in hospitals and other workplaces during this and future outbreaks of contagious disease. It came from the SAFER project on SARS-CoV-2 in frontline health care workers, funded by the UK Medical Research Council, and is written in Python 3.8 on Mesa 0.8.7. It was published by Nick Gotts on CoMSES in August 2021. Coverage: stylised hospital spaces based on one London hospital. Access: free code on CoMSES. Licence: Apache-2.0. Caveats: a prototype with simple spaces, not a calibrated floor plan. Simulation uses are testing distancing rules and space layouts for hospital operation during a pandemic. Related records: the emergency department simulation on CoMSES and the hospital fire evacuation model for GAMA.
